output.narrative_summary: Renew for One Year produced the best outcome in 77% of runs of this model. That result rests on Query Load Growth, which drives Platform Cost, so how that growth plays out is worth watching.

story_headlines.opt_renew: Renew for One Year holds up because Platform Cost stays manageable across most modelled query growth paths.

robustness_explanation.summary: The ordering holds in about 88% of variations, and overall confidence in this comparison sits at 74%.
robustness_explanation.primary_risk: Query Load Growth feeding into Platform Cost is the main thing that could change this picture.
stability_factors: The result stays consistent across most of the modelled range for Query Load Growth.
fragility_factors: The link from Query Load Growth to Platform Cost is the one relationship that could shift the outcome if growth runs higher than modelled.

output.readiness_rationale: This comparison is settled enough to act on: Renew for One Year holds up strongly, though Query Load Growth is not yet fully evidence-backed and is worth firming up before you close it out.

fac_query_load.specific_action: Pull recent query volume trends from warehouse usage logs to firm up the growth estimate before renewing.
fac_query_load.rationale: Platform Cost is directly driven by this factor, so a better read on growth sharpens the whole comparison.
fac_query_load.decision_hygiene: Estimate expected query growth yourself before checking the usage logs.

key_assumptions: The link from Query Load Growth to Platform Cost assumes current pricing and scaling behaviour continue unchanged.
